At the outset, learned counsel for the appellant seeks withdrawal o f I.A.
No.21102/2023 , which is first application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant- Pankaj Saket.
Accordingly, I.A. No.21102/2023 is dismissed as withdrawn.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is heard finally.

The appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 14.6.2023 passed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50648 2 CRA-11226-2023 by the learned Ist Additional Sessions Judge,
Amarpatan, District Satna, M.P. in S.C. No.25 of 2020, whereby, appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:-

sentences.text: Reading from the evidence of the prosecutrix PW-1, it is pointed out that in Para-3 she admitted that her Mama was having an altercation with the appellant - Pankaj Saket on account of payment of wages when her Mama had threatened Pankaj Saket to entangle him in a false Police Case, if he insists on payment of wages.
It is also pointed out that the victim had admitted that the date on which incident allegedly took place she had not narrated the incident to her Nani for the whole night.

3. PW-2 stated that there is neither any forensic evidence nor medical NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50648 3 CRA-11226-2023 evidence to support the contention of the prosecutrix and infact it is a case of false implication on account of non-payment of wages due to the appellant.
4.
Shri Manas Mani Verma, Learned Government Advocate supports the impugned judgment and prays for rejection of the appeal.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, PW-8 Dr. Pooja Singh has stated that on external examination, no injury marks were found on the body of the victim.
There were no injuries on her private parts.
A pink colour underwear was brought in a sealed condition alleging that it contains blood stains but she had not opened that packet.
This witness has accepted that no definite opinion was given by her in regard to commission of rape.

In para-9, Dr.
Pooja Singh had opined that victim had informed her that Pankaj Saket used to touch her private parts.

Her report is Ex.P-3.
6.

In cross- examination Dr. Pooja Singh accepted that there were no injuries on any of the parts of the body of the victim and she has further accepted that name of Pankaj Saket was given by the victim and her Nana.

7. Ex.P-3 is the medical-examination report as was conducted by Dr. Pooja Singh (PW-8) in which it Pankaj Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13881235/
2 is clearly mentioned that no sign of injury seen over the genital region. U.P.T. negative.

sentences.text: X-ray long bone advised for age determination.
There is no x-ray report available on record.

However, it has come on record that date of birth of the victim was 21.5.2013 as is mentioned in Ex.P-8 and her Dakhil Kharij Register NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50648 4 CRA-11226-2023 Ex.P-9-C.
8.
The victim PW-1 in her statements stated that the incident took place on 4.9.2020 whereas report was made on 5.9.2020.
The victim has admitted that house of the accused is by the side of her house.
She has alleged that the appellant had fingered her private parts as a result she started bleeding.
There is no forensic report available on record to substantiate bleeding faced by the victim.
On the contrary, PW-8 has admitted that she had not seen the sealed packet.

Therefore, in absence of any medico legal or F.S.L. report to substantiate blood stains on the underwear of the prosecutrix coupled with the fact that no injury marks were found by the Lady Doctor during her examinations,
coupled with the fact that PW-1 victim has admitted that there was a dispute between her Mama and Pankaj Saket in regard to payment of wages, and her Mama had threatened Pankaj Saket to involve him in a Police Case, when the prosecution case is neither medically substantiated nor there is any other evidence to substantiate the prosecution case whereas on the contrary the medical evidence given by Dr. Pooja Singh (PW-8) supports the case of the defence that the appellant has been falsely implicated as has been admitted by PW-1-victim that her Mama had threatened the appellant to falsely implicate him in a Police Case, we are of the opinion that this is a case of false implication as prosecution has failed to substantiate the charge through medical evidence where appellant has been falsely implicated.
Prosecution has failed to prove its case.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50648 5 CRA-11226-2023 9.
In view of such facts that the prosecution has failed to prove its case, conviction, on the basis of surmises and oral testimony of the victim alone is not sustainable in the eyes of law.
10. In view of above discussion, the impugned judgment dated 14.6.2023 passed by the learned Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Amarpatan, District Satna, M.P. in S.C. No.25 of 2020 is set aside.

12. The case property be disposed of as per judgment of the trial court.
13. The record of the trial court be sent back.
